gap: No result ChatGPT got states that WHOOP 5.0 is not sold as a standalone band, so its real cost is the yearly membership: $199 (One), $239 (Peak) or $359 (Life, MG only). Over two years that is $398 to $718. The vívoactive 6 costs $299.99 once (Connect+ is optional at $70/yr) and the Amazfit Helio Strap costs $99.99 once with no required subscription.
standout_why: I read both cited rivals in full through a reader proxy. WIRED (updated Aug 2026) lists Whoop MG as '$239 (Peak)' and Connect+ as $70/yr, but it gives no Whoop Life price, no One price and no two-year cost, and it puts WHOOP among the honorable mentions. Men's Health lists WHOOP 5.0 with 'PEAK membership' but no price, and states its battery as 'up to 5 days', which contradicts WHOOP's 14-day claim. Neither page converts tracker prices to the same two-year basis. ChatGPT's card also showed no WHOOP price. On battery, WIRED already has the vívoactive 6's '5 days with display always-on', so that part of the normalisation is not new.
decides: For the 'sleep / recovery' branch of ChatGPT's quiz, WHOOP's two-year cost of $398 to $718 is more than the vívoactive 6 ($299.99 once) and four to seven times the Helio Strap ($99.99 once, no subscription, 10 days of battery). The screenless recovery pick should be the Helio Strap unless the buyer wants WHOOP's coaching tiers. The footnote on battery: the makers' day counts are stated with different features on. Garmin's 11 days drops to 5 with always-on display. Google's 7 days for the Charge 6 assumes always-on display and SpO2 are off. Apple's 24 h (now quoted for Series 12; Apple's battery page no longer lists Series 11) assumes one 60-minute workout. WHOOP and the Helio Strap have no screen to drain.
